description_aosta_valley:
The smallest region of Italy, on the border with France and Switzerland, is dotted with the highest peaks of the Alps such as the Matterhorn, Monte Rosa, Gran Paradiso and his majesty Mont Blanc.
An ideal destination for winter sports lovers, with skis on your feet here you can only have fun, with its green valleys and fairytale castles, the Aosta Valley is an enchanting place to experience all year round.
origins and historical notes on the aost: Origins and historical notes on the Aosta Valley

Inhabited since the fourth century BC by the people of the Salassi, the territory of the Aosta Valley was conquered by the Romans in 25 BC who founded Augusta Prætoria Salassorum, the current Aosta, where the imposing Arch of Augustus still stands in memory of that victory.

The roads built by the Romans, such as the Via Francigena that starts from here, favored the passage of the Goths, the Franks and the Lombards until the arrival of Umberto I Biancamano who, in 1302, transformed it into a duchy, granting the population ample autonomy.
Entered the Kingdom od Sardinia in 1847, Aosta Valley obtained the special status of the Italian Republic in 1948.

The Forensic Cryptoporticus, part of the ancient forum still perfectly preserved, is located under the Cathedral which stands a few steps from the large Émile Chanoux square.

what to see in aosta valley4: Towards the border with France, dominated by the 4,807 meters of Mont Blanc, you can enjoy the scenic and natural beauty of La Thuile between glaciers, walks and mountain bike rides on the Little St. Bernard pass.
what to see in aosta valley5: A little further north, near Courmayeur, in summer immerse yourself in the splendid Val Veny with its mejestic glaciers or in Val Ferret with its green walks, the magical Peuterey forest, the lakes of Miage and Cobal and ancient sanctuary of Notre-Dame de Guérison.
unusual places in aosta valley1: If you are in Aosta Valley in search of unusual places you have to start from the capital, Aosta with the <Link href='/views/aosta_valley/aosta/bramafam_tower' className='text-decoration-none color_link'>Bramafam Tower</Link> of the twelfth century, erected along the ancient city walls, and the <Link href='/views/aosta_valley/aosta/early_christian_church_of_san_lorenzo' className='text-decoration-none color_link'>Early Christian Church of San Lorenzo</Link> hidden under the parish church of the Village. Here are the tombs of the 3 bishops who lived between the fifth and sixth centuries.
unusual places in aosta valley2: The <Link href='/destinations/aosta_valley/valpelline' className='text-decoration-none color_link'>Valpelline</Link>, thelongest side valley in the region, is an unspoilt place to walk through valleys, alpine lakes and refuges away from the usual tourist routes.

history and curiosities about aosta1: the history of Aosta dates back to the Nolithic age, when it was accupied by the Celts who merged with the local populations and gave rise to the Salassi. They defended the lands until the arrival of the Romans who, during their rule, built a wide road and some fortresses such as Augusta Praetoria of which roads, aqueducts, bridges remein and the Forensic Cryptoporticus, which in ancient times surrounded the sacred area of the Roman forum. Precisely becauseof the amonunt of Roman monuments in Aosta carefully preserved, the city is counted as the second place in Italy for the number of sites from the era of the empire.
history and curiosities about aosta2: Christianization and barbarization were 2 historical phases that did not spare even the Aosta Valley, until, to put an end to the internal wars between squires of the lands surrounding Aosta, in the face of the prevalence of the County of Savoy, a bilateral pact was signed.

Throughout the valley there are fascinating castles and fortresses left as a legacy by the Savoy lineage.
what to see in aosta: 3 stops not to be: What to see in Aosta: 3 stops not to be missed

The city, whit its overwhelming beauty, is a destination full of points of interest of great importance, starting with its perfectly preserved archaeological sites. Among the many, we show you 4 must-see stops and the main attractions of Aosta.

Aosta and its symbolic monuments: the Arch of Augustus is a monument places along the road that led to the main entrance of the Roman city, the Praetorian Gate. As the name suggests, the arch was dedicated to Emperor Augustus as a sign of Rome's power. The Preatorian Gate, the second stop not far away, had three openings still present: two side openings for pedestrians and a central one for marble, which is now partly visible on the eastern facade

Aosta and its beating heart: A visit to Place Chanoux in Aosta is a must. Located in the center of the city, it is a rectangular sqare clased to traffic and dedicated to the martyr of the resistance Émile Chanoux, killed by the nazis. Surrounded by historic buildings against the backdrop of the Alps, it is the city's living room from which the main streets branch off where you can shop and admire the square you will find the Cathedral of Aosta.

Aosta and archeology: the Forensic Cryptoporticus of Aosta is the fourth stop, ideal for history lovers. A national monument, it is one of the archaeological sites that best represents the city's Roman past: it is a marble gallery that served to regularize the difference in height of the area and connected two temples, one dedicated to Emperror Augustus and the other to Jupiter, Juno and Minerva.

In addition to getting lost in its mountains, unspoiled nature and many historical testimonies, the city offers many attractions for the whole family. There are 3 suggestions for those who want to experience a full holiday:

The <Link href='/events/aosta_valley/aosta/fair_of_saint_bear' className='text-decoration-none color_link'>Fair of Saint Bear</Link>, held on 30 and 31 Jenuary, is an event that sees artists and artisans people from Aosta Valley exhibit sculptures and carvings on wood, iron and leather objects and much more.

A visit to the beautiful exhibitions at Bard Fort, one of the symbols of the region located along the Via Francigena. Its prisons house a path that tells the history of the Fort, but also contains the Museum of the Alps with numerous exhibitions and multimedia workshops for children.
